summary: The focused probe executed successfully but repaired node 5 rather than leaving it stuck: it ended accepted 3 and decided 3, having received one Prepare, one AcceptSync and one Decide with sequence counter 7. That is real counterevidence to the earlier 'no enabled repair' account, but the receipt does not show the order of those messages or what each did to node 5's indices, so it cannot yet distinguish a processed-and-clamped Decide from a Decide rejected as a sequence break. This revision keeps the construction, ready admission event and decision_gap comparison identical and pumps node 5's inbound Paxos messages one at a time, recording up to ten ordered trace entries with the message kind, sequence counter, and node 5's (accepted, decided) pair before and after each delivery. The resulting receipt will show whether the resend was accepted as the expected next message (clamped, then repaired by a separate Prepare/AcceptSync) or rejected outright (sequence-break recovery), which determines how the run-13 stall must be re-explained.
